alt: Counting calls to the input stream for one input with a count on the first line and one value per line after it. A loop that calls input() once per line makes one more call for every line, while a single sys.stdin.read() call takes the whole input at once, so its count stays at one. With a count of 0 both ways make a single call.

steps.caption: The input has 5 lines: a count, then one value per line. One read() call already holds all of them. The input() loop has made 1 call so far, for the count.
The loop calls input() again for line 1, '2': 2 calls so far. read() is still at 1.
The loop calls input() again for line 2, '4': 3 calls so far. read() is still at 1.
The loop calls input() again for line 3, '6': 4 calls so far. read() is still at 1.
The loop calls input() again for line 4, '8': 5 calls so far. read() is still at 1.
Every line is consumed and the sum is 20 either way. The loop made 5 calls and read() made 1, for the same values.

The input has 1 line: just the count, 0. One read() call already holds all of them. The input() loop has made 1 call so far, for the count.
Every line is consumed and the sum is 0 either way. With a count of 0 there is nothing else to read, so both ways make 1 call.
